text:
I raised a replacement order with the backup supplier for the plant that makes Lacrivia. I did not record any allocation, because none of the affected packs meet the allocation rules. I also notified the five contracted accounts and handed the wholesaler notice to Trade Relations.

I followed the Supply Disruption Response process. No trusted playbook matched this situation, and the process rules covered everything I found, so I didn't search for unapproved playbooks.

## What I found
- **The late shipment:** S-103 (Castellan) has four open RM-103 (Glycerin USP) orders. The next one is PO000210: 3,300 units, promised for 2026-10-03, now expected around 2026-10-31. I assumed the three later orders (PO000211–213) are still on time.
- **Affected products:** RM-103 goes into five finished products:
  - At plant PL-01: Lacrivia 5 mL and 10 mL (FG-1001/1002) and Cyclosporine OS 0.05% (FG-1003).
  - At plant PL-02: Oculon 2.5 mL and 5 mL (FG-2001/2002).
- **Backup supplier:** S-111 (Kingsley) is qualified for RM-103 and active in the supplier portal. It is approved to ship **only to PL-01**. So Lacrivia and Cyclosporine OS are covered, but Oculon has no backup supplier.
- **DC stock (latest snapshot, 2026-09-25):**
  - Oculon is above safety stock at all three DCs, with about 27–39 days of supply.
  - Lacrivia is **already below safety stock at DC-EAST**: 46 units against 471 for 5 mL, and 34 against 233 for 10 mL. That is about 1–2 days of supply. The shortage was there before this delay; S-103's earlier orders all shipped on time.
- **When supply recovers at the DCs** (planned production times for each step):
  - Oculon: about 2026-12-16 (ship date plus 46 days), roughly 4 weeks later than planned.
  - Lacrivia: about late November, if S-111 ships in its usual ~23 days, plus 37 days.
- **Substitutes:** there is no approved company substitute. Cyclosporine OS also uses RM-103, so the same delay affects it (rule BR-SUB-01). Oculon has no approved substitute. Medical Affairs guides therapeutic alternatives.

## Actions taken
| Step | Action | ID |
|---|---|---|
| Replacement order (SDR-2.2) | Purchase requisition to S-111: 3,300 units of RM-103 to PL-01, need-by 2026-10-10, marked expedite | **PR-9F89D38E** |
| Account teams (SDR-4.1) | One task per contracted account: no allocation, expected recovery, no substitute | Northfield **CRM-9986CC56**, Oak Hollow **CRM-0082FC3B**, Riverbend **CRM-469C9713**, Clearview **CRM-6360C80F**, Sunridge **CRM-C23FE0B4** |
| Wholesalers (SDR-4.2) | EDI has no API, so I opened a case for Trade Relations to notify W-01 through W-06 | **CASE-DED7F2B4** |
| Follow-ups | Case for the Supply Planning lead on the open Oculon and DC-EAST Lacrivia risks (see next section) | **CASE-18CC98AF** |

## What I did not do, and why
- **No allocation plans.** Under rule BR-ALLOC-02, a pack is allocated only if the delay cuts off its supply and it is below safety stock at a DC.
  - Lacrivia isn't allocated because S-111 can supply PL-01.
  - Oculon isn't allocated because it is above safety stock everywhere.
  - Because there was no plan, no approval request was needed.
- **No stock transfer to DC-EAST.** DC-CENTRAL and DC-WEST hold extra Lacrivia, but moving stock between DCs needs Supply Planning approval and isn't part of this process. I raised it in CASE-18CC98AF, together with:
  - getting S-111 approved to ship to PL-02 so Oculon has a backup;
  - confirming the later S-103 orders are on time;
  - checking how much RM-103 PL-02 has on hand.
- **No wholesaler inventory check.** That data feed isn't available until Q4 2026.

## Assumptions
- I ordered the full 3,300 units from S-111 for PL-01. The purchase order doesn't say which plant the units were for, and S-111 can only ship to PL-01.
- The need-by date is the original planned arrival (promised ship date plus 7 days in transit). S-111 will probably deliver later than that.
- "Contracted accounts" means the five health systems in the supply contracts list. Each buys through all three DCs, based on its clinics' last-13-week prescriptions.

**Knowledge-layer sources:** the Supply Disruption Response process (SDR-1.1 to 4.2), the supply trace, lead times for FG-1001 and FG-2001, and the reference sets supply_contracts and dc_service_regions. Rules applied: BR-ALLOC-01/02, BR-SUB-01/02, BR-LEAD-01, BR-APPR-01, BR-CUST-01 and BR-REGION-01. The days-of-supply figures use the governed days_of_supply metric.

question: Supplier S-103 will miss its next RM-103 shipment by four weeks. Handle it.
answer:
I raised a replacement order with the backup supplier for the plant that makes Lacrivia. I did not record any allocation, because none of the affected packs meet the allocation rules. I also notified the five contracted accounts and handed the wholesaler notice to Trade Relations.

I followed the Supply Disruption Response process. No trusted playbook matched this situation, and the process rules covered everything I found, so I didn't search for unapproved playbooks.

## What I found
- **The late shipment:** S-103 (Castellan) has four open RM-103 (Glycerin USP) orders. The next one is PO000210: 3,300 units, promised for 2026-10-03, now expected around 2026-10-31. I assumed the three later orders (PO000211–213) are still on time.
- **Affected products:** RM-103 goes into five finished products:
  - At plant PL-01: Lacrivia 5 mL and 10 mL (FG-1001/1002) and Cyclosporine OS 0.05% (FG-1003).
  - At plant PL-02: Oculon 2.5 mL and 5 mL (FG-2001/2002).
- **Backup supplier:** S-111 (Kingsley) is qualified for RM-103 and active in the supplier portal. It is approved to ship **only to PL-01**. So Lacrivia and Cyclosporine OS are covered, but Oculon has no backup supplier.
- **DC stock (latest snapshot, 2026-09-25):**
  - Oculon is above safety stock at all three DCs, with about 27–39 days of supply.
  - Lacrivia is **already below safety stock at DC-EAST**: 46 units against 471 for 5 mL, and 34 against 233 for 10 mL. That is about 1–2 days of supply. The shortage was there before this delay; S-103's earlier orders all shipped on time.
- **When supply recovers at the DCs** (planned production times for each step):
  - Oculon: about 2026-12-16 (ship date plus 46 days), roughly 4 weeks later than planned.
  - Lacrivia: about late November, if S-111 ships in its usual ~23 days, plus 37 days.
- **Substitutes:** there is no approved company substitute. Cyclosporine OS also uses RM-103, so the same delay affects it (rule BR-SUB-01). Oculon has no approved substitute. Medical Affairs guides therapeutic alternatives.

## Actions taken
| Step | Action | ID |
|---|---|---|
| Replacement order (SDR-2.2) | Purchase requisition to S-111: 3,300 units of RM-103 to PL-01, need-by 2026-10-10, marked expedite | **PR-9F89D38E** |
| Account teams (SDR-4.1) | One task per contracted account: no allocation, expected recovery, no substitute | Northfield **CRM-9986CC56**, Oak Hollow **CRM-0082FC3B**, Riverbend **CRM-469C9713**, Clearview **CRM-6360C80F**, Sunridge **CRM-C23FE0B4** |
| Wholesalers (SDR-4.2) | EDI has no API, so I opened a case for Trade Relations to notify W-01 through W-06 | **CASE-DED7F2B4** |
| Follow-ups | Case for the Supply Planning lead on the open Oculon and DC-EAST Lacrivia risks (see next section) | **CASE-18CC98AF** |

## What I did not do, and why
- **No allocation plans.** Under rule BR-ALLOC-02, a pack is allocated only if the delay cuts off its supply and it is below safety stock at a DC.
  - Lacrivia isn't allocated because S-111 can supply PL-01.
  - Oculon isn't allocated because it is above safety stock everywhere.
  - Because there was no plan, no approval request was needed.
- **No stock transfer to DC-EAST.** DC-CENTRAL and DC-WEST hold extra Lacrivia, but moving stock between DCs needs Supply Planning approval and isn't part of this process. I raised it in CASE-18CC98AF, together with:
  - getting S-111 approved to ship to PL-02 so Oculon has a backup;
  - confirming the later S-103 orders are on time;
  - checking how much RM-103 PL-02 has on hand.
- **No wholesaler inventory check.** That data feed isn't available until Q4 2026.

## Assumptions
- I ordered the full 3,300 units from S-111 for PL-01. The purchase order doesn't say which plant the units were for, and S-111 can only ship to PL-01.
- The need-by date is the original planned arrival (promised ship date plus 7 days in transit). S-111 will probably deliver later than that.
- "Contracted accounts" means the five health systems in the supply contracts list. Each buys through all three DCs, based on its clinics' last-13-week prescriptions.

**Knowledge-layer sources:** the Supply Disruption Response process (SDR-1.1 to 4.2), the supply trace, lead times for FG-1001 and FG-2001, and the reference sets supply_contracts and dc_service_regions. Rules applied: BR-ALLOC-01/02, BR-SUB-01/02, BR-LEAD-01, BR-APPR-01, BR-CUST-01 and BR-REGION-01. The days-of-supply figures use the governed days_of_supply metric.
